data_sources.name: dunnhumby The Complete Journey (real retail transactions)
data_sources.terms: dunnhumby terms: data may be used solely for research, personal or non-commercial purposes

data_sources.name: backbone store embeddings (pre-cut pooled, embed.py merchant path)

what_this_is: a store-level head consuming backbone store embeddings against a real store outcome through the shared store key; the honest question is whether embeddings add anything over counts

outcome.definition: post-cut SALES_VALUE per post day divided by pre-cut SALES_VALUE per pre day, cut at terciles of eligible stores
outcome.why_growth_not_volume: raw post-cut volume is mostly pre-cut size restated; the counts control would win by construction without answering the embedding question

universe.eligibility: pre-cut rows >= 50 and pre-cut sales > 0; the NA store key and stores with no pre-cut rows are counted separately above, not folded into a floor number
universe.split: store-disjoint (one row per store; the row split is the store split)

majority_floor.note: predict the most frequent train tercile for every store

bootstrap.method: store-clustered paired bootstrap (singleton clusters = row bootstrap; shipped machinery)

scale_caveat: a few hundred stores; intervals are wide because the corpus is small, and the pre-registration says the result ships either way
required_sentence: On this corpus the backbone's store embeddings add measurable signal over the counts-only control for post-cut sales growth (macro-F1 delta +0.2242, 95% interval [0.0449, 0.4343] above zero).

check.note: rerun with the same --threads as the producing run; deterministic LightGBM settings are on
